To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

social facilitation of key pecking by pigeons is observed only when responding is reduced by electric shock, that social stimuli have no effect on the suppression of responding produced by electric shock, and that social stimuli do have an effect on the suppression produced by electric shock.

(a) the presence of another pigeon in a neighboring chamber facilitates responding when responding is suppressed by electric shock but does not affect responding in other situations; and, (b) the effect of shock on responding is greater than the effect of other variables that affect responding in the absence of shock.
social facilitation occurs only when responding is suppressed by shock, and that the effect is proportional to the magnitude of the suppression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of social and non-social stimuli in a situation where the subject is under aversive control.
the interaction of social and non-social influences in a situation where the subject's behavior is under the control of aversive stimuli.
the effects of the presence of other organisms on operant responding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data are not incompatible with the social facilitation hypothesis.
social facilitation is not an all-purpose effect but rather is a specific effect which is sensitive to the level of suppression of the baseline behavior.
conditioned suppression provides a sensitive baseline for the study of social facilitation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of social variables on operant behavior are not simply a function of the rate of that operant behavior.
social facilitation is a special form of the more general effect of social stimulation on operant responding.
social stimuli are more potent in the presence of an aversive stimulus, but only insofar as the aversive stimulus suppresses responding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social facilitation effect is not a general effect that is observed across all types of situations.
the social facilitation effect is sensitive to the baseline level of responding.
social facilitation can occur when a subject's responding is suppressed by a warning stimulus.
